explanation: Option A is correct because the mandatory side is InsuranceCard: every card must belong to a patient. Placing patient_id in InsuranceCard and declaring it NOT NULL enforces that requirement, and making patient_id UNIQUE prevents more than one card from being linked to the same patient. Option B would incorrectly force every patient to have a card. Option C neither places the foreign key appropriately nor enforces one-to-one uniqueness. Option D models a many-to-many relationship, which does not match the business rule.

options.text: Store patient_id in InsuranceCard, declare it NOT NULL, and add a UNIQUE constraint on patient_id
Store insurance_card_id in Patient, declare it NOT NULL, and add a UNIQUE constraint on insurance_card_id
Store patient_id in Patient, allow it to be NULL, and add no uniqueness constraint
Create a separate junction table with patient_id and insurance_card_id as a many-to-many mapping

prompt: A hospital stores patients and insurance cards. Business rules: each patient may have zero or one insurance card, and each insurance card must belong to exactly one patient. Which design best matches this one-to-one relationship while keeping the card's foreign key non-null?
